text:
maria: quick heads-up — finished the continuous-batcher sweep across us-west1 / us-east4 / eu-west1. results are noisy but actionable. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

axel: nice, top-line numbers? p50/p95 and throughput?

maria: p50 (prompt+gen) @ h100-us-west: 42ms / p95 210ms at steady-state, ~8500 tok/s per-GPU for seq=1024, window_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=4096.

jonathan: that's much better p50 than we saw before. what about a100?

maria: a100-us-east: p50 68ms / p95 340ms, throughput ~11k tok/s for long sequences (seq=4096) — A100 wins on throughput for heavy-token workloads, H100 wins for latency-sensitive short-seq.

axel: kernel notes? which kernels were active?

maria: on H100 we used triton_fused_attn + flash_kv, on A100 cutlass_fp16 path was dominant. switching kernels changed p95 by up to 20-30ms on H100.

jonathan: did you run quantized variants? int8 / q4?

maria: ran q4-int8 for a quick pass. perf up ~12% on throughput but observed a small quality regression on the eval set (~0.6% ROUGE drop on one eval). need more eval prompts before enabling by default.

sophia: any fairness issues? last time multitenant jobs saw starvation when a single customer sent long sequences.

maria: yes — default fairness=none led to head-of-queue long sequences grabbing large batches and increasing tail latency for small requests. we tried three modes: fifo, weighted, per-tenant-token-cap. weighted (weight inversely proportional to avg-req-size) improved p95 for small tenants by ~18%.

axel: can you paste the batcher config you used?

maria: sure:
```
batcher:
  window_ms: 12
  batcher_mode: continuous
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_size: 256
  fairness_policy: weighted
  tenant_token_cap: 65536
```

jonathan: good — how sensitive is window_ms? tried 6/12/24?

maria: 6ms gave lower p50 but throughput dropped 8% (smaller packs). 24ms increased throughput ~10% but p95 for short requests doubled in some regions. 12ms is a reasonable sweet spot for mixed workloads.

sophia: region differences — anything surprising for eu-west?

maria: eu-west1 (A100 fleet) had more variable p95s during busy hours — likely noisy neighbors. dedicated pools reduced variance substantially.

axel: thought: maybe implement hybrid scheduler that uses weighted fairness + quick-path for <64 tokens requests (bypass batching or micro-batch).

maria: tried micro-batch bypass for <32 tokens — p50 improved by ~30% for those requests, overall throughput unchanged. caveat: slightly higher GPU scheduling churn.

ci-bot: job benchmarks/1779012345-h100-us-west finished: 36 tests, total 48m. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1779012345-h100-us-west/ (logs + charts).

jonathan: can you attach the latency/throughput charts? want to review for sizing proposal.

maria: uploaded charts + csvs to the job artifacts. key chart: p95 vs batch_window_ms across kernels. also added kernel-selection heatmap per region.

axel: for capacity sizing, what's conservative tokens/s per GPU to use for our cost model?

maria: recommend using: h100: 7.5k tok/s (mixed/mid workload), a100: 10k tok/s for long-seq heavy workloads. subtract 15% for peak headroom.

sophia: action items?

maria: 1) run broader int8 eval on prod-like prompt suite (jonathan)
2) prototype hybrid scheduler (axel) with micro-bypass for <64 tokens
3) run dedicated-pool stability test in eu-west (sophia)
4) update capacity spreadsheet with conservative tok/s (maria)

jonathan: I'll start the int8 eval tonight. linking prompt set and expected metrics in the job.

axel: will sketch hybrid scheduler config, aim to keep policy pluggable.

sophia: I'll queue the dedicated-pool run for tomorrow morning (off-peak).

maria: thanks all, if anyone wants raw data ping me and I'll share subsets. :thumbsup:
